correctness.rationale: For n=4r+2>=6 and m=n/2 odd, each translated length-5 cycle has an odd number of frustrated (equal-spin) edges; summing gives 2f-e_i>=n, and two odd inner m-cycles force e_i>=2, yielding f>=m+1 and minimum energy H/J=2f-3n>=-2(n-1). The 8-state transfer matrix T(z) with state (a_i,b_i,b_{i-1}) and edge cost [a=a’]+[c=b’]+[a=b] exactly enumerates labeled configurations by tr T(z)^n. Normalized determinant det(I-y z^{-1}T(z)^2) has E0=(1-3y²+y^4)^2, E1=-2y(y-1)^2(y^4+8y^3+15y²+8y+1); its logarithmic trace derivative has odd-y coefficient 2m² F_m at z^1, attaining the lower bound. Independently recomputed E0/E1 via 8x8 determinant symbolic arithmetic (both identities true), and independently verified the weighted determinant identity. A fugacity w^{a+b} yields odd-y first correction -2y^7+(2-w²-w^-2)y^5-2y, restricting magnetization to 0 and ±4 and giving coefficient A_m=m[t^((m-5)/2)](1-3t+t²)^(-2) for ±4. Independent transfer dynamic programming directly gave totals 36,250,1274,5508 and respective ±4 counts 0,5,42,225 for n=6,10,14,18. The determinant identity plus odd-cycle bound, not finite checks alone, supports all odd m.

value.rationale: The graph family GP(4r+2,2) is a standard sparse cubic graph with two frustrated odd inner cycles. Its exact all-size ground-state energy, degeneracy 2m²F_m and complete magnetization-resolved count are natural statistical-mechanical observables. These closed forms are substantially more informative than a generic transfer matrix or one isolated dodecahedral computation and can benchmark frustrated Ising calculations.

limitations: No claims for n odd, n divisible by four, temperature, unequal coupling or external field.
The known n=10 degeneracy and general Potts transfer matrix are prior art, not newly established.
